headline: Karnataka HC condones 23-day GST appeal delay, remands with 10% deposit and ₹15,000 cost
reference: C S Sathyanarayana v. Commercial Tax Officer, WP No. 109536 of 2025 (T-RES), Karnataka High Court (Dharwad Bench), 20 November 2026, NC: 2026:KHC-D:19343
summary_points: Issue: First appeal against a ₹58,21,712 GST demand (FY 2017-18) was rejected at admission for a delay of 23 days, with no medical proof of illness.
Held: The delay of 23 days was condoned and the appellate order dated 23.10.2025 set aside. The appellate authority must decide on merits as per Section 107(11) and (12).
Court relied on Bondada Engineering (WP 26900/2024, 20.03.2025), treating rejection of the statutory first appeal on a technicality as denial of a substantial right.
Remand is conditional: deposit of an additional 10% of the tax liability and ₹15,000 cost to the PM Emergency Relief Fund within two weeks.
Proof of deposit and cost is a precondition to hearing. The petitioner is to appear on 08.12.2026, and disposal is expected within two months of the first appearance.
who_is_affected: Taxpayers whose GST first appeals were dismissed for short delay or non-appearance, and the appellate authorities handling such appeals in Karnataka.
action_required: Taxpayers with similar rejections may consider a writ petition, but should be ready to pay the additional deposit and costs and to appear on the dates fixed; verify the full order before relying on it.

Karnataka High Court (Dharwad Bench) has set aside the dismissal of a GST appeal filed 23 days late.

The petitioner faced a demand of ₹58,21,712 for FY 2017-18. The appellate authority rejected the appeal at the admission stage, as there were no medical records to support the delay and nobody appeared at the hearing.

The Court condoned the delay and remanded the matter, following the Bondada Engineering ruling. The appellate authority must now decide the appeal on merits under Section 107(11) and (12), with reasons.

The relief comes with conditions:
- Additional deposit of 10% of the tax liability
- ₹15,000 cost to the PM Emergency Relief Fund within two weeks
- Proof of both is a precondition to hearing on merits

The petitioner is to appear on 08.12.2026, and disposal is expected within two months of the first appearance.

Takeaway: courts may lean towards a justice-oriented approach on statutory first appeals, but expect conditions attached.
